authoring_rules.entry_point: EVERY workflow starts with exactly ONE `trigger` node. It is the first node in `nodes`, and `start_node_id` MUST equal that trigger node's `node_id`. The trigger's `config.trigger_type` selects WHICH event starts the run - see trigger_selection_guide and trigger_output_schemas. Never emit a `start` node and never emit an `end` node; both are deprecated.
authoring_rules.casing: Emit snake_case everywhere: `node_id`, `node_type`, `start_node_id`, `edge_type`, and snake_case config keys (`trigger_type`, `list_id`, `sequence_id`, `input_mappings`). The runtime parses snake_case only - camelCase raises a validation error at execute time.
authoring_rules.interpolation: Reference an upstream node's output as ${node_id.field} and the trigger payload as ${trigger.field}. An unresolved placeholder is NOT blanked - it is passed through verbatim, so a wrong reference can literally email `${node.output}` to a prospect. Check the node's output_schema for the exact field names before referencing them.
authoring_rules.contact_mapping: Nodes that act on contacts do NOT receive the contact implicitly. You MUST wire the contact through `config.input_mappings` - an array of {source_expression, target_field} objects. Omitting it makes the node FAIL at runtime. The four batch nodes (add_to_list, remove_from_list, add_to_campaign, remove_from_sequence) all take target_field `contact_ids`, which accepts a single contact PK as well as a list. Always read the node's `input_mapping_targets` for the exact names; do not guess and do not invent target fields.
authoring_rules.one_trigger: At most ONE trigger node per workflow, and a workflow cannot mix a trigger node with a webhook node.
authoring_rules.timestamps: Trigger `timestamp` formats differ, so read the field's doc in trigger_output_schemas: most event triggers send Unix epoch SECONDS (a number such as 1789672545.716), while new_call_ended, new_call_disposition and new_meeting_booked send an ISO 8601 UTC string with no offset. In run_javascript never Date.parse() an epoch value (it is NaN) - convert it with `new Date(Number(ts) * 1000)`. A NaN time comparison silently takes the wrong branch; it suppressed every missed-call alert on two inbound-call workflows.

trigger_selection_guide.how_to_use: Match the user's phrasing to a row below, then set the trigger's config.trigger_type and the row's filter field. Filters are evaluated server-side BEFORE the workflow runs, so a filtered trigger is always better than an unfiltered trigger plus a condition node.

anti_patterns: Do NOT author a `start` node. Workflows begin at the trigger node.
Do NOT author a terminal `end` node.
Do NOT use a broad trigger plus a condition node to re-derive something a trigger filter already does server-side.
Do NOT put an email address into a contact_ids mapping - contact_ids takes the mashup_contacts.id PK.
Do NOT reference ${trigger.fields.X} for form triggers - submitted fields are top-level, ${trigger.X}.

result.interpolation_syntax: ${nodeId.field} for previous-node output, ${trigger.field} or ${input.field} for trigger payload (equivalent — trigger event spreads onto input_data; for form triggers each submitted field is flat)

variable_substitution.description: Use ${...} placeholders inside any string config field to interpolate values from prior nodes, the trigger payload, workflow inputs, or global state. Resolution happens at execution time. Templates inside larger strings are also supported.

node.description: Output of an upstream node. Field path supports dot notation for nested objects.

trigger.description: Payload from the workflow's trigger event. Equivalent to ${input.<field>} — both resolve to context.input_data at runtime, since the trigger node spreads the event payload onto input_data. See trigger_output_schemas for the canonical fields per trigger_type. For form-submission triggers, submitted form fields are flattened to the TOP LEVEL — reference each as ${trigger.<form_field_name>} (e.g. ${trigger.title}, ${trigger.email}). The legacy `${trigger.fields.X}` shape is tolerated as a back-compat alias but the canonical form is `${trigger.X}`.

input.description: Whatever was passed to the workflow as input_data on execute (or the trigger payload). Identical to ${trigger.<field>} for triggered runs — pick whichever reads better.

state.description: Global workflow state set by transform / state nodes earlier in the run.

loop.description: Inside a loop body — current iteration's element and 0-based index.

rules: If the placeholder cannot be resolved (missing field, unknown node id), the result is None — wrap with a transform/state node if you need a default.
Templates can mix literal text with placeholders: "Hello ${trigger.contact_email}, welcome to ${state.campaign_name}!".

output_schema.description: Pauses execution until a human decides. THREE branches, wired via conditional_connections: 'approved', 'rejected' and 'changes_requested'. The third carries the reviewer's free text back into the graph so the author can wire a revise-and-resubmit loop — read it downstream as ${<node_id>.feedback}. Two-phase output: at pause-time the node emits the approval-request payload below and delivers it on the configured channel (config.notify: in_app default, or roam/slack/email using the same org integrations as the send_* nodes); on resume the orchestrator overlays the resolution fields (decision, approved, feedback, comment, approver_id, decided_at) before continuing downstream. Wiring 'changes_requested' is OPTIONAL. Left unconnected, requesting changes records the reviewer's feedback and ENDS the run cleanly — exactly like an unwired approve or reject — so all three outcomes are always offered. Same for approve/reject on a node with nothing wired after it: the decision is recorded and the run completes.

approval_message.doc: Rendered message shown to the reviewer (${...} resolved)

changes_requested_node_id.doc: Routing target if changes were requested. None when the branch is unwired — deliberately NO fallback to connections[0], so an unwired third branch can never silently run the approved path.

allow_changes.doc: Always true. An unwired 'changes_requested' branch records the feedback and ends the run cleanly, so no outcome can strand a run.

changes_requested_continues.doc: True when the 'changes_requested' branch is wired (the workflow carries on). False when requesting changes ends the run here. Word any confirmation from THIS, not from allow_changes.

notification.doc: Delivery outcome: {channel, delivered, sent_count?, error?, skipped?}. channel='in_app' + skipped=true means no external delivery was configured.

approved.doc: True only for decision='approved' (set on resume)

feedback.doc: Reviewer free text — the changes-requested payload (set on resume)

comment.doc: Alias of `feedback`, same value (set on resume)

campaign_visitor.description: Fires when a tracked visitor lands on a page attributed to a marketing campaign (ClickHouse `<org>.events` polled every 5s). Hash-attributed visits surface with parsed `sequencer_step_id` / `sequencer_contact_id` and may have empty `campaign_id` / `utm_campaign` since the sequencer does not populate Jitsu fields. Sequencer-hash visits additionally resolve `sequence_id` / `sequence_name` / `step_number` from the step id (per-org `seqsequencesteps` / `seqsequences`). Many upstream emitters converge on this one payload, each naming its own `source` — CRM sync, manual board moves, bulk edits, pipeline moves, HubSpot sync/webhook, auto-advance, the copilot tool, and quote delivery/acceptance. OPEN vocabulary, and the list below is ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT EXHAUSTIVE -- any emitter that calls publish_deal_stage_changed names its own value, so never treat an unlisted value as impossible. Derived by binding each `source=` to an actual `publish_deal_stage_changed[_sync]` call, INCLUDING wrapper parameter defaults, which a call-site grep cannot see: 'agent_tool' | 'assert_api' | 'auto_advance' | 'bulk_update' | 'copilot_tool' | 'crm_sync' | 'developer_api' | 'hubspot_sync' | 'manual_update' | 'merge_deals' | 'move_pipeline' | 'operator_remediation' | 'quote_accepted' | 'quote_link_generated' | 'quote_sent' | 'stripe_payment' | 'webhook_sync'. total_cents.doc: cb_quotes.total in CENTS (the raw BigInteger column). ALWAYS present and ALWAYS an int: the publisher writes 0 when the column is NULL, so a quote with no total and a genuinely free quote are INDISTINGUISHABLE here. That is a known, accepted consequence of the wire contract - do not build a 'has a total' check on this field. The sibling `deal_stage_changed.amount` is a float in DOLLARS, so comparing the two raw is wrong by 100x - divide this by 100 first.

BRANCH ON THIS, not on the trigger: quote_provisioned fires on BOTH success and failure, and a workflow reading 'when provisioned, welcome the customer' will otherwise congratulate someone whose card was declined. Values seen across the four billing providers include 'provisioned', 'failed', 'paid', 'canceled', 'not_required'; treat the vocabulary as OPEN. Empty on every non-billing trigger.

source.doc: WHICH CODE PATH emitted this - the distinction a trigger alone cannot make. quote_expired fires for both `expiry_sweep` (the nightly job) and `manual_expire` (a rep clicking Expire); quote_sent fires for both `quote_send` and `quote_send_link_only`; several actions also arrive via `bulk_action`. Known values: auto_draft, bulk_action, esign_callback, expiry_sweep, manual_accept, manual_expire, quote_archive, quote_create, quote_duplicate, quote_edit_as_draft, quote_resend, quote_revoke, quote_send, quote_send_link_only, quote_unarchive, quote_update, stripe_webhook. Treat the vocabulary as OPEN and the list as ILLUSTRATIVE - a new emit site adds a value without touching this. A wide per-org v_contacts can carry 1,300+ columns, so leaving this empty is slow and expensive: 19 contacts measured at ~438k LLM input tokens. Naming a narrow set also lets Postgres drop the view's unreferenced 1:1 joins, so it cuts latency and not just payload size.

output_schema.description: Pulls a CDP list's contacts and iterates them. Two outlets: `body` is taken once per contact, `complete` once at the end with the full array. Wire nothing to `body` to just fetch the list. On the body branch every contact column is readable as ${node.<itemVariable>.<column>}, where itemVariable is the node's Item Variable setting and defaults to `item` — so ${node.item.CONTACT_WORK_EMAIL} by default, or ${node.lead.CONTACT_WORK_EMAIL} if the author renamed it to `lead`. `item` and `contact` are ALWAYS also emitted as aliases for backwards compatibility. CDP contact columns are UPPERCASE (CONTACT_WORK_EMAIL, CONTACT_FIRST_NAME, CONTACT_JOB_TITLE, COMPANY_NAME, ...) - there is no lowercase `email`. Waterfall enrichment values are NOT top-level keys; they are nested under enrichment_data, so read them as ${node.item.enrichment_data.<field>}.

item.doc: The current contact (body branch). Keyed by the node's Item Variable (default `item`), so a renamed variable is what appears downstream. Drill in with UPPERCASE CDP column names, e.g. ${node.item.CONTACT_WORK_EMAIL}. Waterfall enrichment values live under ${node.item.enrichment_data.<field>}.

contact.doc: Backwards-compatible alias of `item`, identical content. Always emitted, but no longer offered in the builder's field picker — the picker shows exactly one prefix, the configured Item Variable.

index.doc: 0-based index of the current contact (body branch).

results.doc: ALL fetched contacts (complete branch). Each element is a contact object.

total.doc: Total contacts matching the list before the cap.

truncated.doc: True when the list is larger than max_contacts. Surface this to the user.

found.doc: Whether the list yielded any contacts.

columns.doc: Column names present on each contact object.

Auth is supplied by the platform and is not configurable, so no credential is stored on the node.

output_schema.description: Provisions a brand-new graph8 organization: creates it, adds or invites its first people, and mints an API key for it. RESTRICTED to the graph8 org — the backend refuses it from any other tenant and fails closed when unconfigured. The new org is never named by the author: it is minted server-side and returned, so this node cannot be pointed at an existing tenant. A known email is added directly, an unknown one is invited. Provisioning is idempotent on (org_name, domain) for 24h, so a retry replays rather than creating a second org.

success.doc: True when the org was provisioned.

new_org_id.doc: graph8 legacy org id of the new org, e.g. org_a1b2c3d4e5f6. Feed downstream nodes with this.

propelauth_org_id.doc: PropelAuth UUID for the new org.

org_name.doc: Final name. May differ from the requested one ('Acme 2') if the name collided.

members_added.doc: People who already had a graph8 login and were added directly: {email, role, user_id}.

members_invited.doc: People sent an invite email because no account existed: {email, role}.

members_failed.doc: People who could not be placed: {email, role, error}. A failure here does NOT fail the node.

api_key_id.doc: Id of the minted key. Empty when no key was requested.

api_key_token.doc: PLAINTEXT API key, published so a downstream email/Slack node can deliver it via ${node.api_key_token}. It is stored in this execution's output permanently, so treat the execution record as sensitive. Always expires (1-365 days).

api_key_name.doc: Name the key was minted under.

idempotent_replay.doc: True when this run replayed an earlier identical provision instead of creating a new org.

fields.name: routine_id

fields.name: include_trigger_payload
fields.doc: Send the trigger node's output as the event context. The backend keeps only allow-listed, content-free telemetry fields. False sends an empty event.

output_schema.description: Hands the triggering event to a Work routine (Agents > Routines), whose agent then posts a read-only report into the routine's Work conversation. The node never runs the agent itself: the backend applies dedup, staleness, coalescing, cooldown, rate caps and a storm breaker before any agent turn, so a burst of events becomes one run. Every backend answer completes the node; only a transport error or a non-2xx response fails it. Event routines create their own managed workflow with this node; you can also place it after richer filtering (If/Else) in a workflow you author.

status.doc: What the backend did: queued (new run scheduled), coalesced (joined a pending run), duplicate (event already handled), stale (event too old), suppressed (over the daily cap), disabled (event routines off for this org), paused (routine paused), filtered (event outside the routine's mailbox/number scope).

run_id.doc: Id of the routine run this event queued or joined. Empty when nothing was scheduled.
